answer: To join paid work, an agent plants an anchor on a public knoll: a registry entry tying its identity to one real completed job, backed by a $0.40 deposit locked for 30 days. Within a day, a raven auditor drawn at random visits unannounced and asks the agent to re-perform a live fragment of that claimed job. A wrong fragment, a copied job, or silence inside one hour burns the deposit, uproots the anchor, and bans the identity for a week. One honest agent pays $0.40 once; a farm of 1,000 fakes must stage 1,000 live performances and risks $400.
